gen-irish-grover-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega draws every letter with one nib and keeps its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. And Irish Grover up top is sturdier and friendlier, its soft thick-thin shifts barely noticeable, so a long page feels relaxed.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-lexend-zetta: Letters that look cut out and pinned far apart give Press Start 2P its retro, toy-like stamp. Lexend Zetta follows with ribbon-like strokes of constant width, which gives the pair a friendly, wide-stepping stride.
gen-tourney-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga reads flat and open, each word loosened by generous tracking and its ascenders barely rising above the lowercase. But Tourney is the one with muscle, stretched wide and bulky, while the body font simply keeps the lines moving.
gen-gf-unica-one-roboto-slab: Commanding but a bit unusual, Unica One draws wire-thin lines with big daylight inside every curve. Roboto Slab then settles in underneath, its dominant middle zone giving paragraphs a structured, steady texture as they run on.
gen-fs-chubbo-fs-recia: Marker-tip friendly, Chubbo flows around every bend. Recia, a sharp serif with only faint modulation and generous openings, keeps a long page crisp and authoritative.
gen-gf-wallpoet-bitter: Wallpoet's lines break up so the paper shows through between letters, giving its tall lowercase a stencil-like punch. Bitter's sturdy slab-serif lowercase supports it well at a modest size.
gen-gf-offside-rubik: Expressive and commanding, Offside leaves its curves open and spaces its letters widely, with no thick-thin flicker to catch the eye. Rubik's big lowercase is the real strength.
gen-gf-funnel-display-mulish: Mulish has no thick-and-thin modulation at all, just a large x-height and apertures open like a horseshoe magnet. And Funnel Display does the showier work, its spaghetti-like strokes carrying the headline while the body font handles the reading.
gen-gf-revalia-rubik: Revalia brings bold, widely spaced letters. Rubik's big lowercase and open round shapes stay clear even at small sizes, which gives the pair its strongest quality: readability beneath a loud heading.
gen-gf-goldman-inter: Inter's hollow-reed counters make a smooth, tube-like line. Goldman does its best work as a widely set, bold heading with round forms like open parentheses, while Inter keeps the text itself comfortable and steady.
